theme: Inspectable metric architecture for the Indus living atlas
question: How can the existing city maps become interactive metric city contexts and detailed building models while preserving the distinction between published dimensions and missing survey geometry?
outcome: Seven offline orbitable models cover two city contexts and five building scenes, with 49 feature records, 590 mesh parts, 3,269 polygon faces, source cards, Plan view, cutaway and optional roofs or water, assumed-height sensitivity and seven metric OBJ exports. All 769 deterministic geometry/source/export checks and 32 browser checks pass. Counts describe the display; no inscribed-object coverage or archaeological confirmation claim is added.
challenge: Incomplete phase-keyed plans and registered city coordinates prevent survey-complete cities. Source prose and a table disagree on Dholavira's city length, and a deep local reservoir probe must remain separate from general basin depth. An initial syntax error and Canvas polygon occlusion broke earlier display endpoints.
remedy: Use named district patches without invented city blocks; preserve source ranges, exact locators and separate footprint, placement and height fields; use native WebGL depth buffering and triangle-depth picking; preserve all earlier endpoints, inspect every model and verify exported geometry independently of the writer.
retry_when: Acquire registered, phase-keyed city plans, building sections and elevations, especially exact reservoir floor and stair geometry, gateway sections and city street coordinates. Replace a named assumption with those observations; another seed or an invented house grid supplies no new archaeological evidence.

authors.model: GPT-6 family; exact serving variant unavailable
authors.role: delegated architecture, source records, procedural geometry and author verification
